**Your microphone on the PC, with any host.** Talk in Discord or in-game voice chat through your phone or tablet while you stream, with Vibepollo, Sunshine or Apollo as they are. No different host needed.

### Microphone
- Turn it on in **Settings → Sound & vibration → Send my microphone**. Starwire sends your voice to a small receiver on the PC, which plays it into a free virtual microphone (VB-Cable).
- Set up the PC once with **Starwire-Microphone-for-Windows.zip** below: unzip it and double-click `setup-microphone.cmd`. It installs VB-Cable from VB-Audio, sets up the receiver (no window, just an icon by the clock), starts it when you sign in and checks it works. Then pick **CABLE Output** as the microphone in Discord or the game. [Step-by-step guide](https://github.com/SicarioGaming/Starwire/tree/main/windows#readme).
- Starwire turns on the device's echo cancelling and noise reduction where it has them. If teammates still hear the game, wear headphones.
- Home network only: the audio isn't encrypted, so Starwire only sends it to a PC on your home network or over a private VPN like Tailscale.
- Running [logabell's Apollo build](https://github.com/logabell/apollo-microphone/releases)? Choose **The PC's streaming app** instead and the microphone goes over the stream itself. Thanks to logabell for that code.

### Phones and foldables
- Settings now show on narrow screens. On a phone held upright or a Galaxy Z Fold's cover screen they were blank.
- The game screen fits phones: a smaller cover and title, and the Play and settings buttons stack.
- The top of the game screen scrolls away with your games. On a phone held sideways it used to fill most of the screen. Once it's gone, a slim bar keeps the selected game and its Play button at the top; tap the bar to scroll back up.
- On a phone held sideways, the stream menu puts Close, Quit and Disconnect on one row, so more tools fit.
- On a foldable's inner screen, the stream follows how you hold it instead of forcing landscape, which could leave it small with black borders.

### Game screen
- A Quit button sits beside Resume while a game is running, so you don't have to long-press the tile.
- Games without cover art each get their own take on the Starwire tile (colour, ring, moon, glow) instead of all looking the same.
- Softer corners, covers that arrive one after another and give a little when you press them, and a gently floating cover. The screen's animations pause while you stream.

### Settings and the stream menu
- Settings that change latency, smoothness, picture quality or battery have a short **Impact:** line under them, so you can see what turning one on or up gains or costs.
- The floating menu button is smaller, see-through until you touch it, and closes the menu as well as opening it.
- Menu items that switch something on or off (Stats, Mouse mode, Keyboard, Pan and zoom, Touch sensitivity, On-screen controller, Menu button) show a small switch, and tapping them keeps the menu open.
- The menu header shows the game's cover art. Desktop and games without cover art get a Starwire tile.
- The Lite stats line uses plain words: data rate, ping, decode time, dropped frames and FPS.

### Fixes
- Tapping a running Desktop tile to reconnect no longer crashes the app (the Resume button already worked), and neither does long-pressing Desktop or another icon tile. Create shortcut now works for them too.

### Install
Download **Starwire-0.2.0.apk** below and open it. It installs over 0.1.2 and keeps your pairing and settings.

GPL-3.0.
